review_type: Author analytic, numerical and instructional review; not independent certification

reviewed.reasoning: Reviewed the completeness axiom versus derived results, nested-interval extraction, finite-coordinate subsequences, Cauchy criterion, sequential closedness, compactness equivalences with a nested-box open-cover proof, boundedness and attainment of extrema, uniform continuity, spectral construction via Rayleigh extrema and invariant-complement induction, uniform limit/finite-integral/derivative interchange conditions, M-test, complete bounded-function spaces, full Banach fixed-point proof with a priori/posteriori/residual and perturbation bounds.
reviewed.deferred_proofs: Supplied both previously saved obligations in full: real symmetric spectral decomposition; local C1 implicit-function existence and uniqueness on a shared complete ball, root Lipschitz dependence, Neumann inverse bounds, total differentiability and continuous derivative. Also constructed the local inverse map. Earlier chapter references now link to exact proof anchors.
reviewed.arithmetic: Exact rational geometric tails, polynomial integrals and tolerance thresholds; independent Simpson limiting integral; rational nonlinear fixed-point iterates compared with independent bisection and closed form; residual/step/perturbation bounds; spike integrals; harmonic block differences; affine fixed-point errors; eigenprojector reconstruction; implicit-system roots and finite-difference response; explicit small-ball constants.
reviewed.solutions: Eight exact prompts independently solved, including proof and hypothesis critique. Open-versus-closed domains, parameter ranges, repeated eigenvalues and singular root collisions explicitly handled.
reviewed.instruction: Defines supremum, subsequence, metric, open/closed sets, compactness, uniform norm, contraction and operator norm before relying on them. Proofs use prior calculus, linear geometry and elementary sequence arguments; general infinite-dimensional compactness is explicitly excluded from finite-dimensional claims.
reviewed.sources: MIT analysis resource PDFs and author-hosted Lebl method sections retrieved. Further-reading links are primary teaching/author sources, not certification of original manuscript or numerical examples.
reviewed.structure: Two fully worked examples, eight exercises and complete solutions, teach-back and delayed check, sources, cross-references and explicit scope.
